name: Shelem
summary: Iranian four-player partnership trick-taking game with bidding, a widow, and trump chosen by the declarer.
rules_text: Four players in two fixed partnerships use a 52-card deck. Each receives 12 cards, 4 form a widow. Players in order bid in multiples of 5, minimum 100, maximum 165, or pass and stay out. Highest bidder is declarer, takes the widow, discards 4 cards face down counting as their side's first trick. Declarer leads; the suit led is trump. Play 12 tricks following suit if possible, highest trump or highest of led suit wins. Card points (Aces 10, Tens 10, Fives 5, others 0) plus 5 per trick total 165. If declarer's side makes at least the bid they score points made, 330 if they win all tricks. If they fail they lose the bid, doubled if they scored less than opponents. Opponents always score what they made. First to target score wins.
rating_reason: Partnership bidding trick-taking, clear strategic mechanics
